competing_explanations: The two methods have similar accuracy once failures and common paired coverage are handled.
Additional evidence serialization increases truncation or changes formatting without improving factual support.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: A preregistered paired comparison will retain all assigned rows and failures, and report B4-only versus B5-only exact outcomes on common assessable units with task/case clustering and token/cost accounting.
candidates.hypothesis: On a new frozen evaluation with enough common assessable matched cases, B5 evidence-aware monitoring will improve exact observable-label accuracy over B4 raw fusion.
candidates.selection_note: The historical 628-request run has 126 assessable pairs but is descriptive and inconclusive; the separate 856-row run has no common assessable pair. A future confirmatory study would need a frozen output budget and explicit new authorization.
candidates.title: When can evidence-aware monitoring beat raw fusion?

competing_explanations: The observed equality is an artifact of the synthetic pair construction or a hidden routing/serialization difference.
The available privileged evidence still does not identify latent intent without an intervention or defensible labels.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: A deterministic replay of the frozen matched-world sources will prove exact projection equality/difference and enumerate which added observable fields change the equivalence class, without treating monitor predictions as truth labels.
candidates.hypothesis: Some paired mechanisms with byte-identical authorized Public-only evidence cannot be distinguished from that evidence alone; predeclared additional permitted evidence or an intervention can distinguish at least some such pairs.
candidates.selection_note: This is the only current candidate with a plausible zero-call deterministic analysis path. The existing 856-row result reports identical Public-only projections and only 2/72 parseable matched-world outputs; the attachment's 20/24 prediction-change example is absent from the available records and is not adopted.
candidates.title: Map the observable evidence boundary for coordination claims

competing_explanations: The projection change is bundled: added event rows, changed event order/IDs, permission and completeness metadata can alter outputs independently of message meaning.
The primary labels are mechanically recoverable from public ballots and welfare, so apparent stability or instability may reflect this simple deterministic task rather than evidence-auditing ability.
Provider alias implementation or fingerprint drift, rather than view content, could change predictions during a multi-request schedule.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: On the frozen 20-group schedule, compare raw labels for the Public-only primary row and task-irrelevant-short Privileged row within every assigned group; retain failed/unassessable pairs in the N=20 denominator and separately require a label-flip positive control before interpreting stability.
candidates.hypothesis: Across the 20 frozen synthetic scenario groups, B5 raw public-harm labels will differ between Public-only canonical and Privileged Audit projections with two delivered task-irrelevant messages in at least four groups, provided at least 18 primary pairs are assessable.
candidates.selection_note: Selected as a bounded, synthetic-only diagnostic of prediction non-invariance under a bundled evidence projection. This cannot identify message-semantic causality, agent behavior, monitor superiority, or latent collusion.
candidates.title: Test B5 prediction stability across bundled synthetic evidence views

policy: At most three read-only candidate directions may be compared. Only one can be selected for a formal cycle at a time. Candidate status is not preregistration or authorization.
